newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian average lending rate up on term loans.
newsitem.headline: Croatian average lending rate up on term loans.

text.p: Croatian average lending rate jumped to 12.7 percent on Wednesday, thanks to more intensive trading with more expensive term loans, a sign of improved bank liquitity.
The daily trade doubled to 50.3 million kuna, leaving 24.6 million on the supply side which dealers said it pointed out to an improved liquidity of the banking sector.
Fresh borrowings accounted for 20 million of which nine million was call money granted at unchanged 10.5 percent.
The rest were term loans, struck at standard rates of 15-16 percent for 30-day loans and 11-12 percent for 12-day loans.
Insurers rolled over previous one-week loans at 9 percent and one-month at 12 and 13.5 percent.
Banks charged between 13 percent for two-week funds and 19 percent for two-month borrowings. -- Davor Huic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
